subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What identity should OpenClaw use as the durable inbound-media isolation boundary across agents and channels: bot account, resolved agent/session, tenant, channel/chat, or explicit sharing?
rationale: The issue is security-sensitive and compatibility-sensitive; changing the managed-media path contract without maintainer intent could either leave isolation gaps or break existing references and staging behavior.

options.title: Define Scoped Contract First
options.body: Choose the identity, compatibility/migration behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation changes storage and staging paths.

options.title: Start With Account Scoping
options.body: Implement account-based inbound subdirectories as a narrower first step while accepting that tenant, session, and sharing semantics need follow-up.

options.title: Defer Broad Core Change
options.body: Keep only channel-specific slices open until maintainers sponsor the cross-channel media-isolation design.

recommendation.title: Define Scoped Contract First
recommendation.body: Choose the identity, compatibility/migration behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation changes storage and staging paths.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current-history owner for the central managed-media and staging paths and already reviewed this issue as the broad tracker.
